notes: The kept set covers population genomics (1,011 yeasts, human innate-immunity selection and archaic introgression, million-year-old mammoth DNA, plant pan-genomes), experimental evolution (LTEE), speciation (genomic grey zone, fish speciation rates, wild tomato radiation), adaptation and convergence (paleognaths, pandas, fruit ripening, nodulation), genome evolution (WGD, Lepidoptera chromosomes, a supergene, HGT, mito/nuclear rate variation, Ne and adaptive substitution), phylogenomics of major clades and the archaeal/Asgard roots of eukaryotes. One somatic-evolution paper (dN/dS selection in cancer) is kept as a borderline case because its result is a molecular-evolution measurement. The shortlist is skewed toward phylogenomics and microbial HGT, so the set lacks sex-chromosome and transposable-element/genome-size evolution, mutation-accumulation and Drosophila work, and classic adaptation systems such as sticklebacks or Darwin's finches.
